public_rationale: Anthropic reported improved behavioral control in December 2022 and alignment improvements with limits to generalization in May 2026 [e1, e3]. A December 2024 experiment demonstrated alignment faking under constructed training conditions [e2]. The July 2025 theoretical results concern external filtering under computational assumptions, not every LLM-based alignment method [e4]. These items establish neither an independently validated LLM-only alignment solution nor an impossibility result covering the claimed class, so they leave the forecast unresolved [e1, e2, e3, e4].
limitations: The experiments do not establish reliable alignment across all relevant deployment settings.
The filtering results do not rule out methods that change model architecture or weights.
The claim specifies neither a deadline nor precise definitions of alignment and permissible auxiliary components.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that LLM-based methods cannot by themselves produce AI that reliably follows intended human goals and safety constraints across relevant deployment settings.
Solve means a robust solution, rather than improved results on selected safety tests.
Alone restricts the proposed solution's technical scope; it is not a separate future antecedent that must occur before the claim can be evaluated.
Ordinary training data, human-specified goals and LLM-based feedback are not automatically excluded. A solution depending on a separate non-LLM mechanism would not falsify this claim.
criteria.support_condition: An independently validated impossibility result establishes that the relevant class of LLM-based methods cannot solve alignment under assumptions matching the ordinary reading.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A publicly documented, independently validated solution achieves reliable alignment using LLM-based methods alone across the relevant deployment settings.
